notes:
Summary: Pylon is a payments/marketplace platform that personalizes offers in-flight; latency is business-critical (checkout conversion). Primary ask: sub-100ms p50 for ranking calls, cost sensitivity at scale. Strong interest in Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching profiles, prefix KV caching to minimize repeated context compute, and aggressive quantization (8-bit/4-bit) if fidelity holds.

Call notes / snippets: • CTO Anika Rao: "We see conversion drop when ranking latency climbs — need predictable tail behavior." • SE: Mateo ran initial mock and saw 2-3x cost saving potential with prefix cache + small batching windows.

Security / deployment: Pylon requires VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; primary constraint is EU data residency for EU customers — want option to pin EU region. They asked for audit logging and a retention policy for logs.

POC acceptance criteria (as discussed): 1) Perf: p50 <80ms, p95 <200ms for 95% of observed traffic pattern; 2) Cost: at least 30% reduction vs current in-house infra after batching/caching; 3) Quality: model output within tolerance (A/B vs FP32 baseline) after 8-bit quantization for ranking models.

Stubs / artifacts: pricing deck in Drive, security FAQ submitted to legal (drive link above), Fireflies meeting ids for tech calls. Jira RDW-1123 is placeholder for a small infra issue raised during bench prep.

Sales notes / tone: Hungry for a predictable cost story — good expansion potential if POC passes. Keep communications short and technical; push bench results and token-level cost breakdown.

Next steps (short): - Redwood to provision Dedicated test pool + run 48-hr benchmark (date 3/16) - SE to deliver quantization candidate and baseline metrics - Legal to complete residency signoff (Pylon legal)

Open questions: Who owns KV cache warmup during traffic bursts? How to do graceful degrade to smaller model variant on overload?
